# Databases

## Core ideas and reasoning

A database is an organised collection of related data. A relational table represents one type of entity; each row is a record and each column a field. Choose data types according to values and operations, such as text for identifiers with leading zeros and numeric types for quantities. A primary key uniquely identifies a record and cannot be null. A foreign key refers to a candidate or primary key in a related table, supporting relationships and referential integrity. Do not duplicate all parent details in every child record: separating students and registrations reduces inconsistent updates. Queries select, join, filter, sort or aggregate data. Forms support entry and viewing; reports present formatted output. Validation rules enforce permitted values, but access control and backups protect different risks. A one-to-many relationship permits one class to contain many students while each student belongs to one current class in that model. State assumptions because real systems may allow enrolment in several classes. An index speeds selected searches but takes storage and update work; it need not be the primary key.

## Worked practice

### Example 1

Distinguish a field from a record in a student table.

A field is one attribute such as surname. A record is the collection of fields describing one student.

### Example 2

Explain why admission number can be a primary key if it is unique and always present.

A primary key must identify exactly one record and cannot be null. A unique, present admission number meets those conditions; a surname may repeat.

### Example 3

What is the purpose of ClassID as a foreign key in a student table?

It links a student to a class record. Referential integrity can prevent an unknown ClassID from being assigned, avoiding orphan references.

## Check your reasoning

Explain why the method applies before calculating or naming a result. Compare with a contrasting case. For calculations carry units, keep intermediate precision, then check by substitution, conservation or a second route. Describe observations separately from their explanation.
